product.description: Icirc;n vara anului 1914, cea mai mare parte a Europei s-a prăbușit intr-un război atacirc;t de catastrofal incacirc;t a zdruncinat politica și insuşi sistemul de credinţe al continentului intr-un mod fundamental. Dezastrul i-a inspăimacirc;ntat pe supraviețuitori și a șocat o civilizație care iși asumase total rolul de model pentru restul lumii. Totul s-a prăbușit intr-un haos de o sălbăticie aflată dincolo de orice termen de comparație. Icirc;n 1939, europenii aveau să inceapă un al doilea conflict care a reușit să fie chiar și mai teribil ndash; un război in care uciderea civililor a ocupat scena centrală și care a culminat cu Holocaustul. Drumul spre iad ne spune această poveste cu ințelegere, fler și originalitate. Kershaw reia evenimentele intr-o narațiune fascinantă, dar abordeaz și problemele cele mai dificile pe care le ridică aceste intacirc;mplări din trecut ndash; ce au insemnat ele pentru europenii care le-au declanșat și care le-au trăit și ce inseamnă pentru noi. Istorie la dimensiuni epice... ar trebui să figureze in lista lecturilor obligatorii. ndash; The New York Times Ne aflăm in prezenţa unui istoric emerit. ndash; Spectator Magistral. ndash; The Economist Ian Kershaw este autorul lui Hitler 1889-1936: Hubris și al Hitler 1936-1945: Nemesis, volume care au primit Wolfson Literary Award pentru istorie și Premiul Bruno Kreisky din Austria pentru cartea de politică a anului. De asemenea, a mai scris Making Friends with Hitler, care acacirc;știgat Elizabeth Longford Prize pentru biografie istorică, Fateful Choices: Ten Decisions that Changed the World, 1940-44, și The End: Germany 1944-45. Ian Kershaw este considerat unul dintre experții de frunte ai lumii in istoria Germaniei naziste și in personalitatea lui Adolf Hitler. Membru al Academiei Britanice și al Societății Regale de Istorie, a primit titlul de cavaler in anul 2002, pentru serviciile aduse in calitate de istoric.

# The Road to Hell: A Definitive History of World War II and the Holocaust

Immerse yourself in one of the most profound and unsettling narratives of modern history with *The Road to Hell*. By acclaimed historian Ian Kershaw, this book offers an epic, deeply researched account of the collapse of civilization and the catastrophic events that reshaped Europe during the 20th century. This essential read provides more than just a timeline; it is a powerful exploration of human behavior at the brink of disaster.

***

## The Descent into Crisis: A Global Narrative

The story begins with the monumental upheaval of the summer of 1914, when much of Europe plunged into World War Iâa conflict of such devastating scale that it fundamentally shattered the political and social structures of a continent. The aftermath was a period of staggering chaos, leaving surviving civilizations shocked and unprepared for what lay ahead.

The narrative progresses dramatically to 1939, covering the second global conflict. *The Road to Hell* details a war unique in its focus on the systematic murder of civiliansâa darkness that culminated in the horrors of the Holocaust. Kershaw masterfully guides the reader through these devastating events, offering not only historical understanding but also profound reflection. The book tackles the most difficult questions: What did these atrocities mean for the European people who instigated them, and what does this history signify for us today?

This is a monumental work of non-fiction history that demands attention from anyone seeking an in-depth, comprehensive look at modern global conflict.

## Meet the Expert: Ian Kershaw

The authority behind *The Road to Hell* is Ian Kershaw, who stands as one of the world's foremost experts on Nazi German history and Adolf Hitlerâs role in history. His scholarly work is renowned for its depth and clarity.

Kershaw is a distinguished historian and a member of the British Academy and the Royal Historical Society. His other acclaimed works, including *Hitler 1889-1936* and *Hitler 1936-1945: Nemesis*, have earned him prestigious accolades such as the Wolfson Literary Award for History and the Bruno Kreisky Prize in Austria.

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Is this book purely academic?**
While the content is based on rigorous historical research, Kershaw writes with exceptional narrative flair. The book is structured as a highly readable and engaging story rather than a dry textbook.

**Does it cover only World War II?**
No. *The Road to Hell* situates the events of 1939 onward within the context of the initial collapse following World War I, providing a comprehensive view of European instability.
